63bfd6813bd6ea90.title: PARP1 hyperactivation uncouples transcription from protein expression through nuclear RNA retention.
digest: The DNA damage response triggers widespread transcriptional changes and modulates protein degradation, yet its role in regulating translation remains largely unexplored.
Here, we uncover that hyperactivated PARP1 suppresses global mRNA translation by inducing nuclear RNA retention.
Mechanistically, we find that APE1-dependent cleavage of abasic sites drives PARP1 hyperactivation, leading to translation arrest in human cells.

93242dacdb30dd43.title: Lifestyle and Metformin Interventions and Risk of Multimorbidity in Individuals With Prediabetes
digest: To the Editor A recent study documented the long-term health benefits of the 25-year-old Diabetes Prevention Program (DPP).

Results demonstrated that the highly motivated DPP cohort derived significant benefit from the original intervention’s 16 individualized, hour-long health coaching sessions during 6 months, reinforced by monthly group and individualized follow-up meetings during the next 1.5 years.

However, when the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention later assumed management of the program, this staff-intensive individualized coaching was eliminated for budgetary efficiency, altering a motivationally core feature of the intervention.

c05ba9946620a435.title: Cassidy sets key vote on Overton, even as he remains undecided on nominee to lead FDA
digest: WASHINGTON — The Senate health committee has scheduled a pivotal vote for next week on the nomination of Heidi Overton to serve as commissioner of the Food and Drug Administration — despite lingering doubts from Republicans on the panel.
The vote is set for Nov. 18, according to a committee release.
If it passes, Overton’s nomination would then go to the full Senate, where Republicans are racing to confirm nominees before Democrats take power in January.

431eccd5040af86a.title: Comprehensive proteomics reveals stage-specific signatures in blood that precede diabetic kidney disease onset and progression
digest: Diabetic kidney disease is the leading cause of kidney failure worldwide, yet the molecular events underlying disease initiation and progression remain unclear.
We measured 5,420 circulating proteins in 830 adults with type 1 diabetes and examined their longitudinal associations with onset and progression of kidney disease over 10 years of follow-up.
Mendelian randomization prioritized UMOD, SORT1, CLSPN, MAST4 and EGF as potential targets.

cd68cb34f19323a7.title: BMI alternative would flip obesity diagnosis for millions, study finds
digest: LONDON — Millions of people would have their obesity diagnoses flipped — from having obesity to not, and vice versa — if an alternate way of defining the disease supplanted the standard body mass index measure, according to a new study that argues such an approach could lead to better care for patients.
The study, published Wednesday in the journal Nature, is the latest volley in a debate about the limitations of the body mass index, and what could possibly replace it.
